commit.message:
Disable yield-local optimization for sticky VTs, use local+signal for start

The yield optimization (!stickyAffinity gate in afterYield) kept sticky VTs
on the carrier's local FJP queue after Thread.yield(), even when the queue
was empty. This trapped carriers inside topLevelExec (avg 52 tasks/1.25ms
per entry vs 1.7 tasks/0.037ms without), starving external queue scanning.
Handler VT I/O wait times increased from 32ms to 52-71ms.

Revert the yield path to upstream fibers behavior: all VTs (including
sticky) go to the external queue when the local queue is empty.

Change the start path from lazySubmit to pool.execute for sticky callers.
This preserves local queue placement (good for locality) while adding
conditional signaling (good for parallelism on 2-core configs).

Merge upstream/fibers, adapt to lazyUnpark removal

Upstream removed lazyUnpark/lazyStart. stickyAffinity now uses
currentThreadIsSticky() in the start() path to trigger lazySubmit
for FJP locality. The polled() callback uses plain LockSupport.unpark
since the caller's stickiness already triggers lazySubmit in the
VirtualThread.unpark() path. Removed lazyStart() from OfVirtual.
Use VThreadScheduler.currentCarrierThread() test utility instead
of direct field reflection in StickyAffinityTest.

Restore useLazyUnpark dispatch, limit stickyAffinity to mode 3 sub-pollers

Mode 2 sub-pollers no longer use stickyAffinity — they revert to the
original useLazyUnpark dispatch in polled(). Only mode 3 (per-carrier)
sub-pollers are sticky.
Sticky VTs skip externalSubmit in afterYield

Add stickyAffinity() to Thread.Builder.OfVirtual

Virtual threads with sticky affinity preserve carrier locality:
- start/unpark from a sticky VT uses lazy submission (local queue, no signal)
- sub-pollers (mode 2 and 3) are made sticky, simplifying Poller.polled()
